stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries into VLMs.
Utilizes Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to inject high-level geometric priors derived from RGB video data.

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid introduces a new method for controllable video generation.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
It specifically addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex).
The framework allows for training harness-based agents across diverse environments using open infrastructure.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in deep logical reasoning within large audio-language models (ALMs) compared to text-based LLMs.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework.
The framework transfers advanced reasoning capabilities from a text teacher model to an audio-language student model.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models specifically for African languages.
The models leverage the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder and cover 27 language varieties across several African nations.
Training data primarily consists of read speech from religious texts, ensuring broad and license-clear datasets.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical performance bottleneck in speculative decoding when dealing with extremely long contexts (millions of tokens).
The issue stems from Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads running full attention over the entire KV cache during drafting, causing linear cost growth.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' method aims to mitigate this 'Draft-KV Tax' by optimizing how the draft head interacts with the large context.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-emphasized in model explanations, drawing inspiration from counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of simply reducing sycophancy in LLMs.
It proposes that socially calibrated models must learn to distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent moral judgment.
The study identifies three structured dimensions governing how LLMs revise their judgments based on external input.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent performance in visual reasoning, even when problem representations (text, diagram, combined) are equivalent.
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different input views expose complementary but sometimes conflicting reasoning capabilities in VLMs.
This highlights a current limitation in multimodal AI, where strong reasoning in one modality (e.g., text) does not guarantee success in another (e.g., visual input).

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework designed to enhance 3D spatial awareness in VLMs.
The framework integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries, utilizing Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) learned from RGB videos.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across state spaces of increasing dimensionality.
The method achieves this by augmenting the state with conditional noise along an expanding interpolant.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for time-series explanation.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in black-box model interpretations.

stories.title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
stories.author: Maxim Secor
bullet_points: Introduces EnsembleEGNN, a foundation model designed to handle molecular conformational ensembles rather than single structures.
The model uses Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNN) to encode individual conformers, followed by a Set Attention Block for ensemble pooling.
It is pre-trained on CREMP, a dataset focused on cyclic peptide ensembles, addressing a limitation in current molecular property prediction methods.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input views (text vs. diagram).
The study highlights that different views can expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning pathways in VLMs.
The proposed 'MIRROR' method aims to leverage these multi-modal views to improve visual reasoning in AI models.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that uses LLMs to transform static clinical cases into interactive, decision-centered storytelling games for medical education.
Addresses a limitation in current LLM applications in medicine, which often only provide localized interactions (e.g., Q&A) instead of full learning trajectories.
Employs a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to structure and execute complex clinical scenarios.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
It addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
The framework enables training harness-native agents across diverse and complex environments.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research introduces GS-Agent, a method to generate dynamic, physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language descriptions.
It addresses the limitations of traditional computer graphics, which require extensive manual effort for fine-tuning.
The core challenge being tackled is ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in generative simulation models.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent code concepts across different programming languages (Python and Rust).
It employs a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the task, the specific language, and the underlying model architecture on code representations.
The study measures a comprehensive inventory of grammatical concepts (58 for Python, 57 for Rust) to determine if representations are consistent across the experimental conditions.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy constraint of using cloud-based LLMs for coding tasks involving sensitive data.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as a solution to keep data on-premise.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the performance of AI agents on longitudinal data preparation tasks.
